newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: No impact in Far East on genetically-altered beans.
newsitem.headline: No impact in Far East on genetically-altered beans.

text.p: The furore surrounding genetically-altered soybeans has not spread to the Far East, Singapore-based grains and oilseeds traders said on Thursday.
"Who cares?" a senior dealer for a European commodity house told Reuters when asked if buyers around Northeast and Southeast Asia have complained about the beans.
"I think that's more of a European deal than anything else. Buyers here have taken the word of the FDA (Food and Drug Administration) that it's safe," a trader for a U.S. commodity trading firm said.

The beans, developed by U.S. firm Monsanto Co, has run into a blizzard of protests from European environmentalists who claim it is a risky experiment with nature and could harm the health of consumers.
"So far, there has been no reaction here. For buyers here, what's more important to them is price, whether the soybeans they're buying is cheap or not," one trader said.
The soybeans were genetically altered to withstand treatment with Roundup, a weedkiller.
